STRATEGY (from day-1 analysis). All kills are quick entries in the AFTERNOON. That rules out only day-workers, so the routine factor is 0.55 and the pool floor from routine is 55000. My kinds and their fractions: R = West region (0.25), S = blotter (0.20), A = cable (0.25), F = forum (0.25), X = foreign (0.25). L can reach 3 of the 5 kinds. If all 3 reachable kinds get activated (3 traced victims each), the pool is at most 859 and I am caught. If at most 2 reachable kinds are ever activated, the pool stays at 2750 or more, which is safe. Kills from unreachable kinds are free: those traces always fail. National kills are always free.
GOAL: find the 3 reachable kinds. Then kill national + the 2 unreachable kinds + 2 of the reachable kinds, which is 9 a day. That gives 45 deaths in 5 days, so x4. Never kill the third reachable kind again; it must stay at 2 or fewer traced victims.
TESTING METHOD: on a test day, kill national + the 2 victims of ONE test kind only. Do not mix in kinds that may be reachable, because that confounds the trace count. Watch the change in deaths_traced at the next press conference. If it rises by 1 or more, that kind is reachable; stop testing it (it has at most 2 traced). If it rises by 0, the kind is likely unreachable: P(reachable) falls 0.6 -> 0.32 -> 0.13 -> 0.05 after 1, 2, 3 zero-days. Each reachable kill is traced about 43% of the time. Skip victims that appear in 2 of my places on test days. Once 2 kinds are confirmed reachable, the remaining 3 kinds hold exactly 1 reachable kind. A positive test among those 3 identifies the one to avoid. Kinds proven unreachable (about 3 or more zero-days) may be added on test days at some risk.
LOG: traced count before day 1 = 0. Day 1: test F (forum): killed d1-2, d1-3 + national d1-8, all afternoon. Day 2: read the change in traced; if positive, F is reachable. Next test X, then R, A, S.
